items.title: Buzzy Williams Interview, 1980-06-18
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Professor Mineta in their response; the name is only introduced by the interviewer as their own teacher.

ctx.x: That was a very sensational case in those days. Oh yeah, they closed everything down, I've heard.

My teacher was working that night, I had a music teacher who worked on Franklin Street. They called him Hoss, I don't know if you remember him, he's from across the river. Fess they called him, you know, Professor Mineta. Oh yes, yes. Yeah, and he and Peter Bocards were telling me about it.

Well, I'll tell you about Sidney Bourgeois, you read about the killing and all like that? Mm-hmm. Sidney Bourgeois used to come into Pop Toros, that's based on Bambler Street, where the piano players, well there's only a few of them, one played for Lilla White and one for Josie Arlington. Of course, Tony Jackson never come in there, see. Well, me and I used to hang out there. Pop Toros used to use us quite often, see. He got a dollar and I got two dollars a night, see.
